hypotheses.name: Cirque de Gens
supportingClues: All frames form one continuous cliff-jump and rescue sequence at the same river pool.
The sheer pale-limestone walls, wooded plateau, deep green pool, and broad gravel bars resemble Cirque de Gens and other southern French karst gorges.
The rescuers' navy uniforms with a red chest stripe are characteristic of French sapeurs-pompiers.
contradictions: No sign, bridge, village, distinctive arch, or other uniquely identifying landmark is visible.
Several swimming and cliff-jumping sites in the Ardèche, Gardon, and Hérault gorges have nearly identical terrain.

canonicalizationCalls.query: Cirque de Gens, Chauzon, Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, France
